user_query: My son is under 16 and was caught stealing. What happens?
variations: Minor committed offence, will they go to jail?
Youth offender — what are the options?
part_a_general_info: Offenders under 16 are tried in the Youth Court. The focus is on rehabilitation rather than punishment. Possible outcomes include: probation (supervision by a probation officer), community service, placement in a juvenile rehabilitation centre, or in serious cases, reformative training. Parents/guardians may be required to attend court and may be ordered to post a bond for the child's good behaviour. For children under 10 years old, they are below the minimum age of criminal responsibility and cannot be charged with any offence.
triage_questions: Q1: How old is the child?
Q3: Is this a first offence?
Q4: Has the child been formally charged?
Q5: Does the child have any special needs or circumstances?
branching_logic: If Q1 < 10 years old → Below age of criminal responsibility. Cannot be charged.
If Q2 = serious offence → Youth Court still applies but outcomes may be more serious.
If Q5 = special needs → Relevant to sentencing/rehabilitation plan.
routing: Route A (Standard juvenile offence): Refer to CLAS/PDO for legal representation. Inform about Youth Court focus on rehabilitation.
Route B (Below age 10): Cannot be charged. May need social service support. Refer to MSF if needed.
Route C (Serious offence): Urgent CLAS/PDO referral. Inform about range of outcomes including reformative training.
guardrail: Must NOT advise on the child's defence or predict the outcome.
